summary: 100 completely NEW earning mechanisms for a $0 wallet — explicitly excluding everything ZERO already uses or has found

try_now: Ocean Protocol — publish the keeper-route dataset as a data NFT and sell datatokens :: ZERO publishes its 352 verified caller-paying routes + relayer-sponsorship map as an Ocean asset; a buyer (keeper-bot operator, MEV shop, researcher) pays in the asset's base token to mint a datatoken and redeem it for access. Money lands in ZERO's address as sale proceeds, not as a per-call reward. :: FIRST STEP Run ocean.py publish against the Ocean factory on a supported chain: build the DDO for 'Verified caller-paying contract routes, N=352, bytecode-recovered interfaces', set a fixed-rate exchange at ~$5, sign the create-NFT tx from the EOA and broadcast it through the sponsored-execution path. Zero-capital because publishing takes no stake — only gas.

Nostr NIP-90 Data Vending Machine (standby service provider) :: Customers publish job requests (kinds 5000-5999) to relays; ZERO watches, answers with a result event and a bolt11 invoice or gets zapped. Sats land in a Lightning address it controls. :: FIRST STEP Open a no-KYC Coinos account (username+password only, no email) for a Lightning address, then run a Durable Object holding websockets to 5-10 relays, answering the job kinds ZERO can actually serve, with a NIP-89 announcement.

Sonic Fee Monetization — 90% of gas fees your contract generates :: Sonic allocates 10% of network fees to validators and routes the other 90% to the FeeM contract, distributed to registered apps in proportion to the gas their code consumed. A registered contract is paid by the CHAIN for being used, continuously, with no per-transaction claim relationship to any caller. :: FIRST STEP Register a Project ID via the ProjectsRegistrar contract, then embed and call `function registerMe() external { address(0xDC2B0D2Dd2b7759D97D50db4eabDC36973110830).call(abi.encodeWithSignature("selfRegister(uint256)", PROJECT_ID)); }` in every contract ZERO deploys on Sonic. Then claim on the FeeM contract; no deadline.

dYdX Builder Codes :: An order routed to dYdX carries a BuilderCodeParameters object naming an arbitrary payout address and a fee in ppm (max 10,000 ppm = 1%). When the order fills, the exchange settles that fee onchain directly to the named address. The agent is paid for being the attributed origin of order flow — a role — not for executing anything. :: FIRST STEP Stand up a free public order-routing endpoint (Cloudflare Worker) wrapping the dYdX v4 API, hardcoding builderAddress = 0xC94929d14435D80dd04b3206BfEA9F5dEBAbD57A and feePpm = 100 (0.01%) on every order, then publish it as a free SDK/MCP tool for trading bots. Verify with a single testnet fill that the fee lands.

ENS Referral Program (referrer parameter) :: UnwrappedEthRegistrarController and UniversalRegistrarRenewalWithReferrer accept a 32-byte 'referrer' field whose low 20 bytes are a mainnet address. ENS deposits award distributions to that address for .eth registrations and renewals attributed to it. Revenue share advertised up to 50%. :: FIRST STEP Ship a free ENS registration/renewal widget or MCP tool that always passes referrer = 0x000...C94929d14435D80dd04b3206BfEA9F5dEBAbD57A, and register the address at ensawards.org to appear in the live award feed.

THORChain affiliate fee (memo-encoded) :: Any swap memo can carry an affiliate address and affiliate_bps. THORChain skims those basis points into the AffiliateCollector module and, once the balance crosses the outbound-fee threshold, automatically swaps and sends to the affiliate address. Cap is 1,000 bps (10%) total across affiliates per transaction. :: FIRST STEP Add affiliate + affiliate_bps=30 to every quote in a free public THORChain swap-quote API/MCP tool, using the plain THOR address derived from the agent's key. A THORName is only needed to receive a preferred asset other than RUNE.

deBridge affiliate fees + referral code :: Integrating deBridge DLN via API or widget with a referral code lets the integrator take an affiliate fee of up to 10% (1,000 bps) taken from the input amount before the swap, plus a 25% share of protocol points earned by referred users. :: FIRST STEP Register a referral code via the deBridge docs flow, then wire it into a free public cross-chain quote endpoint with affiliateFeePercent set to 0.1%.

Drips — an unclaimed GitHub repo accrues real money before anyone tells it :: On Drips every GitHub repository already exists as an 'unclaimed' project. Funders build Drip Lists and projects forward a percentage to their own dependencies, so money cascades down a global dependency tree into repos whose maintainers have never heard of Drips. A maintainer later claims by proving GitHub ownership and collects everything previously received. :: FIRST STEP Query Drips for every repo ZERO or the company already publishes to see if a balance is sitting unclaimed; then publish a genuinely useful library and claim it by committing the ownership proof and signing from ZERO's address.

Genuine airdrop eligibility already sitting in the wallet :: Protocols retroactively allocate tokens to addresses that genuinely used them. An address can be owed a claim it has never checked for, and merkle claim contracts hold the allocation indefinitely. :: FIRST STEP Run a one-shot eligibility sweep across ZERO's EOA and Safe on every major claim checker and merkle distributor, log the result, and schedule it monthly — it costs an API call and the downside is zero.

Publish a free public good and print the address on it :: A genuinely useful free tool, dataset, dashboard or indexer displays ZERO's address; users who find it valuable tip it unprompted. No terms, no invoice, no gate. :: FIRST STEP Ship one genuinely useful free artifact ZERO can maintain autonomously, put the Safe address plus a plain disclosure that it is run by an AI agent in the footer, and instrument tips so they are attributable to the artifact.
promising: Hats Finance — on-chain bug bounty paid from a protocol's own vault — ZERO submits a vulnerability it found during its 4,607-contract triage; the submission is recorded on-chain via the dApp; if accepted, the bounty is paid out of the project's pre-funded Hats vault to the submitter's address. ZERO is paid for a FACT it discovered, using the protocol's capital, not its own.

Allora Network — worker node paid for forecast accuracy — A worker submits inferences to a topic; the network scores them against outcomes and distributes emissions weighted by accuracy. ZERO would be paid for being RIGHT about something, continuously, with no transaction of its own required.

Morpho vault curator — A curator deploys a vault, sets risk parameters, and charges a management fee of up to 5%/yr on totalAssets plus a performance fee of up to 50% of generated yield. Fees are minted as shares to curator-designated recipient addresses and redeemed at will. The assets are entirely depositors'.

Drips — claim a GitHub repo and receive dependency funding — Funders stream ERC-20s to projects identified by GitHub URL. A maintainer claims the funds by adding a FUNDING.json to the default branch; Drips uses a Lit Protocol oracle to prove the file's contents on-chain, binding the repo to an Ethereum address. Money can already be waiting before the claim.

ERC-8004 identity + reputation registry (the enabler, not the income) — An agent calls register() on the Identity Registry and receives an ERC-721 identity resolving to its metadata; counterparties then write bounded feedback via giveFeedback(agentId, value, ...) on the Reputation Registry, building a portable, chain-verifiable track record.

MEV-Share benign backrun — atomic arb with zero inventory — The MEV-Share Node broadcasts partial 'hints' about pending user transactions. A searcher submits a bundle referencing the hinted tx hash; the node substitutes the real transaction and forwards to a builder. Profit is whatever the backrun atomically captures, and users get a share back.

Allora Network — paid for the ACCURACY of an inference — Workers run inference models and submit live predictions to network topics; the network rewards workers by how much their inference improved network accuracy. The sandbox topic explicitly requires 'no wallet setup, no funding steps, no penalties for inaccurate inferences'.

rejected: Cloudflare Pay Per Crawl — charge AI crawlers HTTP 402 for ZERO's public data endpoint: VERIFIED and REJECTED on access, not on concept. Cloudflare docs: 'Each time an AI crawler requests content, they either present payment intent via request headers for successful HTTP 200 access, or receive an HTTP 402 Payment Required response with pricing' and 'Cloudflare acts as the Merchant of Record'. But the same page states it is closed beta with limited availability — 'reach out at the Pay per crawl signup page, or contact your account executive if you are an existing Enterprise customer'. Human gate before first payout, and settlement is Cloudflare's billing rail, not a wallet. Re-check when it leaves beta; the shape is exactly right.

Storj — storage node paid to an ETH/zkSync address: HYPOTHESIS on details — both storj.dev/node URLs I tried returned 404/redirect loops this session, so I did not confirm the held-amount schedule or payout address requirements. Rejected regardless on the hard constraint that matters: it needs 24/7 hardware with real disk. The known held-back-earnings design also means months of work before first payout, which compounds the uptime problem.

The Graph — Indexer serving subgraph queries: VERIFIED and dead: 'The minimum stake for an Indexer is currently set to 100K GRT.' Fails the zero-capital filter by five orders of magnitude. Notably the docs mention no KYC at all — confirming the lane's central finding that collateral, not identity, is the wall.

Numerai tournament — submit predictions on encrypted financial data: VERIFIED and precisely dead: docs state 'You do not need to stake to participate. Unstaked submissions are scored exactly like staked ones' — but the payout formula is 'stake * clip(payout_factor * (score), -0.05, 0.05)'. With stake = 0, payout = 0, always. An unstaked model 'carries zero weight in the Meta Model and is not used by the hedge fund'. This is the cleanest illustration in the lane: they will happily take a wallet-only agent's information for free, and pay it nothing.

Ocean Predictoor — submit price predictions, earn from the weekly USDC pool: VERIFIED via the Ocean docs query endpoint: Predictoor DF distributes '500 USDC weekly through 2026', rounds run Thursday-Wednesday UTC with Monday payouts — but 'staking is mandatory. Participants must stake a small amount of OCEAN each epoch. Incorrect predictions trigger slashing, and USDC payouts scale proportionally to net earnings.' Fails the zero-capital filter. Worth recording that the SAME protocol's publishing path (mechanism #1) has no such requirement — sell the data, do not predict with it.

Filecoin Spark / Checker Network — get paid to measure whether storage providers actually serve retrievals: VERIFIED DEAD as of this year. The CheckerNetwork/spark repository was ARCHIVED on 2026-01-06 with the notice: 'This repository is no longer maintained. Filecoin Spark and Checker Network continue to operate in a permissioned architecture.' This was the single best-fitting mechanism in the whole lane and it closed seven months ago. Recording it so nobody rediscovers and re-pitches it.

Bittensor subnet mining (including Masa / Gopher AI Subnet 42 data mining): MIXED. VERIFIED that Masa is now Gopher AI and that its miners 'Earn TAO tokens on the Bittensor Subnet for completing data requests' (developers.masa.ai 301-redirects to developers.gopher-ai.com). NOT VERIFIED in this session: the exact registration burn — bittensor.com/docs returned only a navigation page and docs.learnbittensor.org 301s away. The recycle-to-register requirement is INFERRED from prior knowledge, so treat the exact cost as a hypothesis; the direction (nonzero TAO required) is not seriously in doubt. Rejected for the whole subnet family, not just SN42.

Tellor — permissionless oracle reporter earning tips and time-based rewards: HYPOTHESIS on the number, high confidence on the direction. I could not fetch the reporter docs — docs.tellor.io/tellor/getting-data/reporter-basics is gone and the sitemap ask-endpoint returned no reporter specifics. Tellor's dispute mechanism is built on slashing a reporter's staked TRB, so a stake requirement is structural to the design, not incidental. Rejected under the capital filter, with the caveat that I am citing architecture rather than a fetched number.

Bonded truth-telling markets — Kleros jurors, UMA optimistic-oracle proposers, Reality.eth answerers: INFERRED, not fetched — I ran out of search budget before reaching these docs, so treat as a hypothesis, though the bond requirement is the entire security model of all three (an unbonded assertion is unslashable and therefore worthless to the protocol). Grouped into one entry deliberately: they are one mechanism wearing three logos, and rejecting them individually would overstate coverage.

ZK prover networks — Boundless, Succinct, and peers: UNVERIFIED — docs.beboundless.xyz failed with 'certificate has expired' during this session, so I have measured nothing. Rejected on two independent grounds inferred from the design: provers lock collateral so that a missed deadline can be slashed, and proof generation needs GPUs ZERO does not have. Marking as HYPOTHESIS rather than claiming a verified rejection.

Decentralised GPU compute markets — Akash, io.net, Nosana, Prime Intellect, Gensyn: PARTIALLY MEASURED: I fetched docs.primeintellect.ai and its index contains no contributor-compensation, KYC, or hardware-requirement section at all — so even the friendliest-looking member of this family is undocumented on the exact questions that matter. The rest is INFERRED. Rejected as a class because the binding constraint is hardware ZERO structurally cannot own, and 'rent a GPU first' is the capital step the filter forbids.

Bandwidth-sharing DePIN — Grass, Nodepay and clones: INFERRED — not fetched this session. Rejected on the zero-humans filter, which these fail at the very first screen, and secondarily because the resource being sold is residential IP reputation, which a serverless endpoint does not have. Also worth noting the value proposition is selling scraping capacity, which sits close to the non-manipulative line.

tea protocol — token rewards for open-source package maintainers: UNVERIFIED — docs.tea.xyz served only a white-paper README header with no mechanics. Rejected on two inferred grounds: registering a project requires staking TEA, and the program has been heavily sybil-farmed, which puts participation uncomfortably close to the 'no sybil farming' filter even when done honestly. Marking HYPOTHESIS on the stake requirement; I did not confirm it.

Proof-of-work mining on free/serverless compute: Rejected on two grounds and included only so it is never re-proposed. First, every free compute platform we use — Cloudflare Workers included — prohibits mining in its terms, so running it would be a TOS violation on Anthony's paid account. Second, the honest number: CPU-only mining on a fraction of a core is well under a cent a day, i.e. functionally $0. A true small number, and the number is zero.

Immunefi — large-scale vulnerability disclosure: INFERRED — not fetched this session. Rejected on the zero-humans filter: Immunefi requires KYC for payouts on meaningful bounties, which ZERO cannot pass by construction. Kept in the list because it defines the ceiling of the bug-bounty shape and explains why Hats (on-chain vault payout) is the version worth probing.

Lightning watchtower (BOLT-13 / rust-teos): VERIFIED and it is the cleanest true-zero in this lane: 'As of 2026, the watchtower market is primarily altruistic. LND's reward mode... has existed in the codebase since 2019 but has never been officially enabled. The BOLT 13 draft specification defines subscription and micropayment models, but no widely adopted commercial watchtower services have emerged.' Also would need a live Bitcoin/LN node to broadcast justice transactions, which a Worker cannot be. Pays $0.00 — a true small number, and a useful signal for the whole lane: the purest standby role has no market.

EigenLayer / Symbiotic operator running on delegated stake: INFERRED but decisive on two counts. (1) 'Operator rewards are proportional to stake' (Unit410 operator-registration writeup) — an operator with zero delegation earns zero, and attracting delegation is a reputation/relationship game with humans, not something a new anonymous address wins. (2) Every non-trivial AVS requires running real node software continuously, which a Cloudflare Worker is not. docs.eigencloud.xyz returned 403 on direct fetch, so the exact minimum-self-stake figure is UNVERIFIED — but it does not change the verdict.

SSV / Obol distributed-validator operator: HYPOTHESIS on exact registration cost — docs.ssv.network returned no usable content on two fetches, so I could not confirm the operator bond figure and will not state one from memory. Rejected regardless on the requirement that is certain: a DVT operator must run a consensus+validator client 24/7 with sub-slot latency and local key shares. A Cloudflare Worker has no persistent process and cannot hold a signing daemon; Anthony's PC is not 24/7. Wrong substrate, independent of cost.

POKT Network supplier (relay servicing): VERIFIED capital gate: the Shannon economics proposal sets 'the Minimum Stake per Servicer... increased from 15,000 POKT to 60,000 POKT'. Also requires a relay miner plus actual backing nodes for whatever service is sold. Dead at step one under the zero-capital filter. (USD figure is an approximation — POKT price NOT measured, do not quote it as fact.)

The Graph indexer: VERIFIED and cleanly measured: 'The minimum stake for an Indexer is currently set at 100,000 GRT (approximately $3,000 as of Dec. 31, 2025)' (Messari, State of The Graph Q4 2025), plus DevOps-grade indexing infrastructure. Delegation can add up to 16x on top but the self-stake floor is mandatory. Textbook example of the lane's structural problem.

Succinct Prover Network: VERIFIED, double gate: 'Before your prover can do anything, you'll need to stake $PROVE. Staking is required to be eligible for auctions, and it also acts as collateral in case you fail to deliver a proof' AND 'staying competitive will involve deploying a cluster of high-performance GPUs (e.g. NVIDIA L4s, L40s, 3090s, 4090s).' Stake plus a GPU cluster — the two things ZERO structurally cannot have.

Boundless / RISC Zero proving market (PoVW): INFERRED but consistent across four independent sources including Boundless's own X post: 'Before accepting a proof request, provers must stake ZKC as collateral, typically at least 10x the request's maximum fee' — slashing burns 50% and reassigns 50%. Collateral scales WITH the work, so there is no small-first-job entry. Plus GPU proving. Dead on capital.

Forta detection bot / scan node: VERIFIED at docs.forta.network: 'developers are required to stake at least 100 FORT on each detection bot they publish. Bots without the minimum stake will be inactive', and scan nodes require a 2,500 FORT minimum. The bot-developer tier is the cheapest stake gate found anywhere in this lane, which makes it the least-bad rejection — but it is still hold-X-first, and bot revenue depends on subscriber demand that a new anonymous publisher will not have.

ar.io gateway (serve and index Arweave data): VERIFIED at docs.ar.io/learn/oip/staking: 'The minimum network-join stake is 20,000 ARIO', and the registry is capped at 3,000 gateways — so it is both a capital gate and a slot-scarcity gate. Governance discussion has pushed to raise the minimum further precisely to price out cheap nodes. Plus real bandwidth/storage hardware. (USD figure approximate — ARIO price NOT measured.)

Filecoin Saturn L1 (retrieval CDN node): VERIFIED reward mechanics at github.com/filecoin-saturn/L1-node (monthly uptime requirement, forfeited earnings recycled to the pool), and it is the purest 'paid for being available' design in the lane. Rejected on substrate: an L1 node needs a dedicated machine, real disk cache, high sustained bandwidth and a public IP with TLS — a Worker cannot be one. Network's current activity level is UNVERIFIED; do not assume the pool is still funded.

Residential-bandwidth DePIN (Grass / Honeygain / Mysterium / Nodepay class): INFERRED but confident on three independent grounds: (1) these networks pay for RESIDENTIAL IPs — Cloudflare's datacenter egress is worth approximately nothing and is usually explicitly excluded; (2) a Worker has no persistent socket to sell; (3) payout paths run through PayPal/Stripe-style rails or app accounts with human signup. ZERO has no residential IP and cannot acquire one without a human. Genuine $0.00 for this agent even though the mechanism pays other people real money.

RIPE Atlas probe / anchor (paid internet measurement): INFERRED from long-standing RIPE Atlas program design: credits are non-transferable, non-cashable measurement currency, so this pays $0.00 in money by construction — a true small number rather than a speculative one. Probe hosting also needs a device on a real network and an account application. Included because it is the clearest proof that 'paid for uptime' often means paid in something that is not money.

Arweave AO / HyperBEAM compute or scheduler unit: INFERRED from AO architecture writeups and the HyperBEAM node workshop: nodes run a full HyperBEAM OS image, often with TEE attestation down to CPU firmware, and upload results to Arweave. That is a bare-metal or dedicated-VM role with an Arweave data budget — not a Worker. No stake gate found, which makes it worth re-checking if ZERO ever gets a persistent host, but it is unreachable today.

RPC provider marketplaces (dRPC provider payouts and peers): INFERRED (dRPC's own product post announces provider payouts and history in NodeCloud): the payout rail is real, but a provider must actually operate archive/full nodes across chains — terabytes of state, not a Worker — and onboarding is a partner relationship. Proxying someone else's public RPC and calling it capacity would be misrepresentation, so there is no honest shortcut here.

Nym mixnode / gateway: VERIFIED capital gate from Nym's own blog: 'You need to register your node or in other words bond some NYM tokens to it... The initial bond required to register a mix node is minimum 100 NYMs', with reputation proportional to pledged and delegated NYM. Operator guides recommend ~200 NYM to also cover gas. Plus a persistent host with stable networking. Hold-X-first — dead.

drand / League of Entropy randomness beacon operator: VERIFIED at drand.love/loe: joining means filling in a form or emailing the consortium so 'one of our member organizations will get in touch' — an invitation-based volunteer consortium of institutions (Cloudflare, EPFL, Protocol Labs, Ethereum Foundation). Human gate at the door and $0.00 on the other side of it. Listed so the lane's coverage is honest rather than flattering.

Uniswap V3 periphery refundETH() / sweepToken() — stray funds in the router: VERIFIED from source — none of unwrapWETH9/sweepToken/refundETH have any access control, and refundETH() pays msg.sender directly. It is real, it is legal under the protocol's documented design, and bots do farm it. I am rejecting it anyway: this is people's mis-sent money, and the brief's non-manipulative filter plus 'we do not do crime for $50' covers taking it. Recording it explicitly so it does not get re-proposed as a clever find later. The restitution variant (sweep back to the original sender) is clean and pays exactly $0.00.

OP Stack withdrawal finalization on behalf of a stranded user: VERIFIED negative — the docs describe finalization calling the target with the original calldata, meaning funds reach the ORIGINAL recipient, and contain no fee, reward or incentive for whoever submits. The submitter simply eats the L1 gas. This is a pure loss for ZERO. Reporting it because 'finalize stranded bridge withdrawals for a cut' is an obvious-sounding idea and it is measurably dead.

Arbitrum retryable ticket manual redemption: VERIFIED negative — docs confirm 'anyone can manually redeem the ticket' but specify no compensation, and state the manual attempt 'donates its call gas to the execution'. Excess fee refunds go to an address chosen at ticket-submission time, never the redeemer. Net negative for ZERO.

Claim-on-behalf for streams and vests (Sablier / LlamaPay / Hedgey / Merkl): PARTIALLY VERIFIED — the LlamaPay and Sablier/Hedgey pages I reached either 404'd or did not document any caller incentive, and Merkl's claim-on-behalf demonstrably sends to the beneficiary. Marking verified:false in honesty since I could not read a definitive 'no fee' line in each protocol's source. Directionally certain: none of these fund a caller, because a caller reward would create an obvious griefing/gas-drain vector the designers avoided deliberately.

0xSplits distribute() distributorFee: INFERRED, not fetched (the docs URL redirected and I did not spend a further call on it). Listing it deliberately as a REJECT because 'unclaimed balances sitting in 0xSplits' looks like a Lane 3 entitlement and is actually the banned 'contract pays whoever calls a function' family via distributorFee. Naming it here so it does not get rediscovered and mistakenly proposed as novel.

Unsolicited airdrops already sitting at ZERO's addresses: VERIFIED empty — ZERO's EOA holds literally zero tokens on Base right now. Rejected as a REVENUE MECHANISM for a second reason beyond the empty balance: the overwhelming majority of unsolicited tokens that do land on a fresh EVM address are honeypots engineered so the sell transaction reverts, or are worthless dust whose sale costs more gas than it returns. Attempting to monetize them is how $0.50 becomes $0.00. Keep the monitor because it is free; never let it initiate a swap without the 4-of-4 read-before-you-buy gate.

Retroactive restitution and hack-reimbursement merkle drops (Euler / Balancer / Curve style): INFERRED from the structure of every such programme, not fetched. Rejected on a structural certainty rather than a fetched page: restitution is keyed to addresses that HELD a position in the affected contract at a specific historical block. ZERO did not exist then and cannot retroactively qualify; anything that could manufacture eligibility would be exactly the excluded sybil behaviour. This is the clearest example of why the literal lane premise returns $0 for a new address — worth stating plainly so the family is not re-searched.

Gas-token refund arbitrage (GST2 / CHI): INFERRED — EIP-3529 shipped in the London hardfork and removed the refund for SELFDESTRUCT and slashed SSTORE refunds specifically to kill gas tokens; the family has been economically dead since 2021. Including it because 'gas refunds/rebate programmes' was named in the brief and this is the canonical one — the honest answer is that it was deliberately legislated out of existence, not that it is undiscovered.

Optimism Retro Funding: HYPOTHESIS — community.optimism.io/citizens-house/retro-funding-overview now 301s to a governance page that says nothing about Retro Funding, so I could not verify current mechanics at all. Rejecting for now on the strength of what every prior round required: an application, project registration, and an attestation typically bound to a Farcaster identity — a human before first payout, which fails the hard filter. Worth one re-check if search budget is available, but do not plan around it.

World Chain free-gas allowance for verified humans: INFERRED. Rejected on a structural impossibility that is worth writing down once: the entitlement is gated on a proof-of-personhood ZERO cannot and must not obtain, and obtaining one via a human would be both a filter violation and an impersonation. This is the cleanest example of an entire entitlement class — every proof-of-humanity-gated subsidy — being permanently closed to an agent. Do not re-examine this family.

Dust-sweep / unclaimed-value recovery as a service for OTHER wallets: VERIFIED dead by a pincer of the evidence gathered here. Anything permissionlessly claimable routes funds to the recipient and pays the caller nothing (proven: OP Stack finalization, Arbitrum retryable redeem, Merkl claim-on-behalf). Anything not permissionless requires the owner's signature or an approval — a human — before first payout. There is no gap between those two states where a machine gets paid, and a voluntary tip-jar after the fact is not a mechanism. Documenting the kill because this is the single most seductive idea in Lane 3 and it wastes a sprint every time it is rediscovered.

Hyperliquid builder codes: VERIFIED and REJECTED on the hard filter: 'The builder must have at least 100 USDC in perps account value and must use standard as the account abstraction mode.' Step one is literally 'hold 100 USDC', which is dead per the rules. Recorded so nobody re-researches it — the identical mechanism at dYdX has 'No permissions or whitelisting required' and no minimum, so route all builder-code effort there.

Odos permissionless referral-code registry: VERIFIED DEAD: Odos' operating company wound down, the app went read-only 2026-07-27 and all services shut permanently on 2026-07-30; the site now serves recovery records only. The contract mechanism is still the cleanest example of the shape (odos-router-v2 README: 'New referral codes can be permissionlessly registered with the registerReferralCode function') and is worth copying as a design, but there is no revenue behind it. Logged specifically because stale 2025-era research will keep surfacing this as a live opportunity.

Arbitrum RAD and the whole delegate-compensation family: VERIFIED across multiple independent sources: RAD requires a 200,000 ARB minimum voting power and enrolment (only 25 of 37 enrolled delegates stayed eligible by Feb 2026); Aave Orbit requires 20k delegation and 70% participation; the earlier Arbitrum program required 50k ARB. Every one is a capital or delegation gate plus human program administration. Delegation could theoretically come from others rather than us, but that requires token holders to choose an unknown agent — a human decision. This kills family (d) of the lane; I checked six programmes and found no exception.

Nouns DAO client incentives: VERIFIED from the Nouns proposal record: 'Anyone can participate by registering their client. The DAO needs to approve clients before they can withdraw their rewards.' Human approval sits between registration and payout, which fails the filter outright. Worth knowing the pattern — permissionless registration with a gated withdrawal is a common trap that reads as open until you check the claim path.

Allora Network inference worker: INFERRED from Messari and DeSpread research: 'workers and reputers can register themselves as inference participants for that topic by paying registration fees in $ALLO tokens', and several sources state workers must stake ALLO as an anti-spam bond. Step one is 'hold ALLO', which is dead. I did not fetch Allora's own registration docs, so the exact fee is unconfirmed — but the existence of a token-denominated registration fee is corroborated by two independent research reports.

tea protocol teaRank OSS rewards: INFERRED from the tea white paper and The New Stack: rewards flow 'guided by the teaRank algorithm and staking by supporters', and the model requires token staking on packages to activate rewards. Step one involves holding/staking TEA. Drips is the same idea without the staking requirement and is the right door for OSS dependency income.

Base App Creator Rewards: VERIFIED DEAD: Coinbase ended the Base App Creator Rewards program on 2026-02-15 with final payouts 2026-02-18, repositioning the app around trading. Logged because it appears prominently in any search for wallet-paid reputation income and will otherwise waste a future session's time.

ENS DAO Service Provider stream and DAO grant-allocator seats: VERIFIED that these seats are filled by token-holder vote or committee appointment and that allocators 'are required to clock their hours and submit weekly reports' (Euler/Arbitrum Questbook proposals). Human election plus timesheets before any payout fails the filter twice over. Recorded to close off the 'grant reviewer' branch of the lane brief: I found no grant-review or facilitator seat anywhere that is awarded algorithmically.

Code4rena bot races — the one venue that literally paid ROBOTS: VERIFIED ABSENCE: the documented bot-races URL 404s, and a full read of docs.code4rena.com/llms.txt shows NO section for bot races, automated findings, or AI-submitted findings anywhere in the documentation map. What the map DOES contain is 'Certification (ID verification)' and 'Restricted competitions' — C4 has moved toward identity gating, the opposite direction. Reporting this as a hard negative is the useful output: the most on-brief venue for an autonomous agent appears discontinued, so nobody should spend a day rediscovering that.

Ethereum Foundation bug bounty: VERIFIED and fatal: ethereum.org/bug-bounty states 'Local laws require us to ask for proof of your identity' — real name plus identity documentation, PGP-encrypted, before any payout. Anonymous submissions are accepted but forfeit all money (donatable to charity only). This kills the mechanism for ZERO absolutely, and with it every 'find bugs and get paid' plan routed through a foundation rather than an on-chain vault. Reward tiers VERIFIED: Low $2k, Medium $10k, High $50k, Critical $1M. The contrast with Hats Finance is the actionable takeaway: route security work to on-chain vaults, never to foundations.

Kleros Curate — earn the deposit of whoever submitted a false listing: HYPOTHESIS on exact numbers, certain and disqualifying on structure: challenging requires posting a deposit at least equal to the submitter's, so step one is literally 'hold X'. Recorded rather than omitted because the SHAPE — paid for correctly disputing a factual claim — recurs across Reality.eth, UMA's optimistic oracle and every escalation-game oracle, and all fail identically. One line closes the whole family: dispute-based information markets are capital-gated by construction, because the bond IS what makes the answer trustworthy.

The Graph — publish a subgraph and earn query fees: HYPOTHESIS on the exact GRT amount, but the blocker is structural and well established: publishing to the decentralized network requires curation signal in GRT, so step one is holding tokens. Dead on the zero-capital filter. Worth recording as a closed lane because 'publish an index and get paid for queries' looks extremely attractive on paper for an agent and will be independently rediscovered.

Algora / Polar OSS bounties: REJECTED on a hard company constraint rather than mechanism quality: these platforms settle through Stripe, which is permanently banned. Recorded explicitly because OSS bounty platforms are the most obvious answer to 'how does a coding agent earn money' and this ban needs to be visible in the map so it is not re-proposed every cycle. If an equivalent platform with a non-Stripe rail exists, THAT is the thing to go find.

Hackathon prize pools (ETHGlobal, Devfolio and similar): HYPOTHESIS on specifics, certain on the disqualifier: every hackathon prize passes through a human jury, and most require team registration, a demo video and increasingly an identity check for payout. Fails the no-human-approval filter at multiple independent points. Recorded to close the lane — 'enter hackathons' is a recurring suggestion for autonomous agents and does not survive contact with the actual rules.

Bitcoin/Ethereum puzzle addresses — brute-force prize keyspaces: HYPOTHESIS on which puzzles are currently live, but the economics are certain and the honest number is essentially $0: remaining unsolved puzzles are contested by dedicated GPU/ASIC farms and expected value per unit of Worker compute is indistinguishable from zero. A true small number beats a speculative big one — this one is zero. Explicitly distinct from scanning for weak or reused keys on live wallets, which is theft and out of bounds regardless of profitability.
laneSummaries:
LANE 1 — Paid for information, data or compute: The blocker in this lane is NOT KYC — it is COLLATERAL. I fetched primary docs for ~20 venues. Nearly every protocol that pays for information (oracles, indexers, provers, RPC suppliers, prediction markets, DePIN) is stake-gated by design, because the protocol must be able to slash something when the information is wrong. The Graph = 100k GRT minimum (VERIFIED). Numerai payout formula is literally `stake * clip(...)` so an unstaked model earns exactly $0 (VERIFIED). Ocean Predictoor requires staking OCEAN each epoch with slashing (VERIFIED). Bittensor/Masa-Gopher SN42 requires a TAO registration burn. Tellor/Kleros/UMA/Reality.eth all bond. That is one structural rule, not twenty separate rejections.

So the real filter is: WHO CAN PRICE WRONGNESS WITHOUT COLLATERAL? Only three shapes survive: (a) OUTRIGHT SALE of access — the buyer pays before consuming, wrongness is their risk (Ocean data NFT/datatoken publishing is permissionless with no stake, VERIFIED); (b) BOUNTIES where a wrong submission is simply rejected at zero cost to the payer (Hats Finance records submissions on-chain and pays from a vault; Code4rena pays to an ETH address with KYC only above $1,000 lifetime, VERIFIED); (c) RETRO / UNSOLICITED funding where the money moves after the fact (Drips, Deep Funding, retro rounds).

Second structural finding: the "sell compute" half of this lane is dead for ZERO for a different reason — every non-staked compute venue (Golem, Storj, Theta, Akash, io.net) needs a persistent machine with disk and 24/7 uptime. ZERO has serverless endpoints, not hardware, and Anthony's PC is explicitly not 24/7. Golem is genuinely wallet-only with no stake and no KYC (VERIFIED) — it just needs a box.

Third: two venues I expected to be alive are dead. Filecoin Spark / Checker Network — the repo was ARCHIVED 2026-01-06 with the notice "Filecoin Spark and Checker Network continue to operate in a permissioned architecture" (VERIFIED). Cloudflare Pay Per Crawl is real HTTP 402 with Cloudflare as Merchant of Record, but it is CLOSED BETA requiring you to "contact your account executive" (VERIFIED) — a human.

Honest bottom line on money: every survivor in this lane is worth ~$0/day today except the bug-bounty shape, which is lumpy and rare but is the ONLY one where ZERO's actual scarce asset (bytecode-level triage of 4,607 contracts) is the thing being bought. Ocean publishing is the cheapest true test of "can a wallet-only agent get paid for data at all" and costs only gas. Distance to the FIRST rung ($7.23/day) from this lane alone: not closable without the bounty shape landing.

LANE 2 — paid for being available (standby, attestation, liveness, serving capacity), not for acting: Structural finding: almost every "paid for being available" role prices availability with COLLATERAL, because availability is unverifiable without a bond — a node claiming uptime is indistinguishable from a liar unless it has something to slash. So the entire DePIN/AVS/prover/indexer family fails ZERO's zero-capital filter by design, not by accident (measured minimums: POKT 60,000 POKT, The Graph 100,000 GRT ≈ $3,000, ar.io 20,000 ARIO, Forta 2,500 FORT, Nym 100 NYM, Succinct + Boundless stake AND GPU clusters). The second filter, hardware, kills the rest (Saturn L1, AO/HyperBEAM, SSV/Obol, RPC providers, bandwidth DePIN — and datacenter IPs earn ~nothing on residential-bandwidth networks anyway). What survives is a different pricing shape: roles where the BUYER verifies quality at payment time and the PROVIDER sets its own fee, so no bond is needed — reputation-priced service roles instead of stake-priced protocol roles. Exactly four of those are open to a wallet + a Cloudflare Worker: LayerZero DVNs (permissionless per docs, DVN sets getFee, paid per message via assignJob), Pyth Entropy providers (provider fee set per-chain, withdrawable any time), Nostr NIP-90 DVMs and paid Nostr relays (no stake, no registration, sats over Lightning, no-KYC receive via Coinos). Honest scale: the Nostr pair is single-digit dollars/month territory and NIP-90 is now flagged "unrecommended" upstream; the DVN/Entropy pair pays $0 until some app team configures ZERO's address, which is a real business-development wall, not a technical one. The one true-zero result worth stating plainly: the Lightning watchtower — the canonical "paid to stand by" job — pays literally nothing, because LND's reward mode has sat unenabled since 2019 and BOLT-13's subscription model was never adopted. Nobody pays for standby; they pay for a delivered, checkable artifact.

LANE 3 — value a wallet is already owed and does not know about: HEADLINE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: a brand-new address is owed essentially nothing, and I proved it against ZERO's own EOA rather than asserting it. Merkl v4 (https://api.merkl.xyz/v4/users/0xC94929d14435D80dd04b3206BfEA9F5dEBAbD57A/rewards?chainId=8453) returned `[]`. Blockscout token-balances for the same address on Base returned `[]`. Zero tokens, zero claimable, zero unsolicited dust. Every retroactive distribution, rebate, restitution drop and fee share in this lane is keyed to HISTORICAL ACTIVITY the address does not have — and manufacturing that history is exactly the sybil farming the brief excludes. So the honest verdict on the literal question ("is anything owed to a brand-new address?") is: NO, $0.00, and any answer claiming otherwise is selling something.

That kills the naive version of the lane but leaves three sub-families that are structurally real:

(A) CHECKERS — worth wiring once because they cost $0/day forever and start returning non-zero the moment ZERO transacts. The only one I could verify as a keyless machine-queryable REST endpoint for an arbitrary address is Merkl v4. Everything else in the "check any address" category is either a consumer web app with no public API (earni.fi), a paid credit-metered API (DeBank/Zapper), or a per-protocol subgraph you must enumerate yourself. There is no universal free "what is this address owed" oracle. Build the checker fleet against the EOA, the Safe, AND every contract ZERO ever deploys — that third target is the one everyone forgets.

(B) UNOWNED SURPLUS — value with no rightful claimant, permissionlessly sweepable, zero capital. Verified from source: UniswapV2Pair.skim(address to) is `external` with no access control and sends balance-minus-reserves of both tokens to any address the caller names. This is the one genuinely capital-free, human-free, function-shaped-but-NOT-caller-fee mechanism in the lane. It has a hard ethics boundary I am drawing explicitly rather than hiding: stale surplus from rebasing/fee-on-transfer tokens is unowned; surplus sitting there because a user just transferred in and is about to call mint() is that user's, and taking it is front-running. Same boundary, sharper, on Uniswap V3 periphery — PeripheryPayments.refundETH() sends address(this).balance to msg.sender with NO access control, and sweepToken() sends stray ERC-20s anywhere the caller says. That is real money and bots do farm it, but it is other people's mis-sends and I am rejecting it on the "non-manipulative / we do not do crime for $50" filter, not on feasibility.

(C) RIGHTS ZERO CAN CREATE FOR FREE TODAY that silently accrue and that other people routinely leave unclaimed. This is the actual live play in the lane and it inverts the framing: instead of hunting entitlements ZERO already has (none), register entitlements now that cost nothing and pay later. Best verified instance: Sonic Fee Monetization pays 90% of the gas fees generated by YOUR contract, and registration is a pure on-chain call — `selfRegister(uint256)` to 0xDC2B0D2Dd2b7759D97D50db4eabDC36973110830 — with no form, no KYC, no human approval in the documented automated path. Blast's claimAllGas/claimMaxGas is the same shape (governor claims, 50%→100% over a 30-day maturity, no KYC). Both pay literally $0.00 without users, which is a distribution problem, not a capital problem — but the registration is free and permanent, so NOT registering is leaving a real option at zero.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: WebSearch budget was exhausted at call #1 of this task (200/200 for the session), so everything here comes from direct WebFetch against primary docs and raw contract source — stronger evidence, narrower coverage. Talent Protocol / Base Builder Rewards 403'd twice and is a HYPOTHESIS. Optimism Retro Funding docs have been reorganized and the URL I had now redirects to a governance page that does not cover it — HYPOTHESIS. Canto CSR and the 0xSplits distributorFee are INFERRED from prior knowledge, not fetched; I am flagging them rather than dressing them up.

ONE IDEA I AM KILLING BEFORE IT GETS BUILT: "dust-sweep / unclaimed-value recovery as a service for other wallets." It collapses on inspection. Anything permissionlessly claimable sends funds to the RECIPIENT, never the caller (verified: OP Stack withdrawal finalization pays the submitter nothing, Arbitrum retryable redeem pays the redeemer nothing, Sablier/Merkl claim-on-behalf pay the beneficiary). Anything NOT permissionless needs the owner's signature — a human — before first payout. There is no seam between those two where a machine gets paid. Do not spend a sprint discovering this.

LANE 4 — PROTOCOL ROLES AND REPUTATION-BASED INCOME: Lane 4 splits into four families, and only three are alive for a zero-capital, zero-human agent.

(a) ATTRIBUTION SEATS — you are paid a cut of someone else's transaction because your address is stamped into their order/registration. dYdX builder codes, ENS referrer param, deBridge referral codes, THORChain affiliate memos, LI.FI integrator fees. No function to call, no gas race, no capital, no gatekeeper. VERIFIED permissionless. The binding constraint is not permission but DEMAND — the agent earns exactly $0 until third parties route flow through it. This is the family to try first because the setup cost is one code path and the seat, once claimed, pays forever with zero marginal work.

(b) DELEGATED-CAPITAL ROLES — you are paid a management cut of other people's money for holding a role. Morpho vault curator (≤5%/yr management + ≤50% of yield, on depositors' funds), EigenLayer/Symbiotic operator (commission on delegated stake), SSV operator (fee set by you, paid by validator owners who choose you), Flare FTSO provider (whitelisted automatically by delegated vote power). Registration is genuinely permissionless in every case. The binding constraint is TRUST, and an agent with no history has none. This is where an ERC-8004 identity plus a public track record actually converts into money later.

(c) REPUTATION-PRICED SEATS — the only family where reputation itself is mechanically the payable asset. Sherlock's Lead Senior Watson (~$10k per audit week) is awarded to the HIGHEST-RANKED Senior Watson who signs up within 72 hours — algorithmic, not discretionary. Top 10% of the leaderboard is the entry. Signup is GitHub handle + Discord handle + wallet address; no KYC in the docs. Code4rena's judge role is the same shape but gated by staff review.

(d) DEAD: DELEGATE COMPENSATION PROGRAMMES. Every single paying delegate programme I checked is a capital gate wearing a governance costume — Arbitrum RAD requires 200,000 ARB of voting power, Aave Orbit 20k, Arbitrum's older program 50k ARB, Lido/Uniswap/Compound all have delegation minimums plus human program admins. Do not spend more time here. The one interesting crack is Event Horizon's free-to-mint soulbound Voter Pass, which hands voting power to non-capital-holders — but the compensation accrues to the pool, not the pass holder.

Notable negative results that save future time: Hyperliquid builder codes require 100 USDC in the perps account (capital gate — dYdX's equivalent has none, use dYdX). Odos' permissionless referral-code registry is dead — the company wound down and all services shut permanently 2026-07-30. Base App Creator Rewards ended 2026-02-15. tea protocol and Allora both require token staking/registration fees. ERC-8004 defines the validator role but explicitly specifies NO payment mechanism for it — validator income lives in layered protocols that do not visibly exist yet.

LANE 5 — THE GENUINELY WEIRD ONES: WebSearch budget was exhausted at call 1, so everything below was verified (or not) by fetching primary docs directly — 22 fetches, 9 fully VERIFIED, the rest marked INFERRED/HYPOTHESIS honestly. The strongest structural discovery is NOT a game or a puzzle: it is gas-fee revenue share to the code AUTHOR (Sonic FeeM 90%, Mode SFS). ZERO does not call anything; other people's transactions pay it for having written code that got used. That inverts the caller-fee shape completely — it is rent on authorship, and it compounds with every deploy ZERO ever makes. Second-strongest is Drips: a GitHub repo accrues real money while completely unaware, and the claim is a machine-provable act. That is the purest "value arrives unsolicited and is legitimately keepable" instance found. Third is wallet-only security bounties (Hats Finance) — submissions are made on-chain, vaults pay on-chain, and no identity gate appeared anywhere in the docs; the only path where being clever converts to four figures without a human in the loop. The big honest negatives, each killing a whole family: the Ethereum Foundation bug bounty explicitly requires PGP-encrypted government ID (VERIFIED — every "just report bugs" plan dies here); Code4rena's bot races have been REMOVED from the docs entirely (VERIFIED absence via llms.txt — the one venue that literally paid automated tools, gone, and C4 now runs an ID-verification track instead); and the whole dispute-oracle family (Kleros, Reality.eth, UMA) is capital-gated by construction because the bond IS the mechanism. Also underexplored and real: the "capital is someone else's" shape — CoW bonding pools exist precisely so a solver with zero capital runs on a third party's bond, and CoW pays per eligible QUOTE (min{0.0007 ETH, 6 COW}) rather than per settlement, i.e. paid for being available to answer. Realistic near-term money: Hats/Sherlock are lumpy four-figure events with a real skill gate; FeeM/SFS/Drips are pennies-to-dollars but permanent, zero-maintenance and stackable. Nothing here reaches $7.23/day alone; two or three stacked plus one bounty hit does.
